text:
Dom: Heads-up — forecasting a 2.8x GPU traffic spike next Tue 10:00-13:00 in us-west-2 from a partner load test. Want to check autoscaler burst mix and guardrails before we hit it. :eyes:
Erin: thanks, adding to sync. Can we avoid full reserved scale-up? last time we paid a lot in on-demand.
Ben: what’s the forecasted GPU hours and tail latency impact? numbers will drive preemptible vs reserved decision.
Dom: forecast link: https://dash.redwood.ai/gpu-forecast?range=next7d — projected 4k GPU-hours that day, baseline 1.4k. 95p latency SLO is currently 350ms.
Clara: remember us-west-2 has maintenance window Wed — not relevant but regional capacity is thinner. Also image pulls blocked some pods last spike. Might need baked images on node images.
Erin: propose smoothing policy: allow burst (preemptible) up to 25% of pool for <2h, but enforce a steady-state cap at +12% reserved. Also add a warm pool of 60 GPUs (pre-warmed, tainted) to avoid cold starts.
Ben: cost check — preemptible mix (75% preemptible for burst) vs 100% on-demand for the extra 2.6k hours: est cost delta ~$120k/day vs $340k/day if we use on-demand. Need to confirm exact pricing.
Alice: also consider cross-region fallback to eu-west-1 for retries — but that adds egress and latency. Might be a good safety valve for non-interactive batch traffic.
Clara: image pull issue — heatmap shows 60s average container start due to registries. If we pre-pull into AMIs or use image prefetch as init, we can cut warm-up by ~30–40s.
infra-bot: autoscaler:detected spike — sample log: "scale_up: requested 200 gpus, provisioned 90 preemptible, 20 reserved, 90 pending"
Dom: ok action items: (1) put temporary burst guardrail (burst_limit=20% of cluster) (2) create warm pool 60 gpus with pre-baked image (3) scale-down-delay 15m to avoid churn (4) limit individual route burst to 10% to protect SLO.
Erin: tentative autoscaler snippet below — we'll iterate. Please comment quickly if risky.
Erin: ```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  burstAllowance: 0.20      # max fraction of extra nodes allowed for burst
  steadyStateIncrease: 0.12 # fraction added as steady capacity
  scaleDownDelaySeconds: 900
  warmPoolSize: 60
  preemptiblePreference: true
  fallbackRegions:
    - eu-west-1
    - us-east-1
```
Ben: suggests adding a hard cap for burst total GPUs to avoid runaway: burst_hard_cap = 400 GPUs. Also set per-tenant throttles on high-cost routes.
Clara: +1 on hard cap. Also suggest node taints so only specific deployments can use preemptible warm nodes.
Alice: for canary, run the new policy for one hour on a subset (svc=partner-test) during low-impact window and metric watch: token-latency, queue-depth, cost-per-token.
Erin: agree. Canary plan: 09:00-10:00 Tue, target svc=partner-test, monitor metrics for 30m, rollback if 95p latency > 400ms or provisioning failures > 2%.
Dom: I'll open a runbook and set the alert thresholds. Runbook link (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/2025-06-Policy-Canary-Procedures
Ben: quick calc: if warm pool lowers cold start by 35s, we save ~0.2ms average latency across requests due to reduced queueing. But biggest wins are cost smoothing and lower tail.
Clara: operational note — need to pre-bake NVIDIA driver + model cache mounts to the IMAGE. Ops might need a short maintenance to roll images.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for infra-image v2025-06-10 -> 120 nodes (staged).
Dom: final guardrails proposal: burst_hard_cap=400, burst_fraction=0.20, steady_state_fraction=0.12, scale_down_delay=900s, warm_pool=60, canary=1h svc subset. I'll create an RFC and tag @eng-sre. :thumbsup:
Erin: I'll queue the CFR and monitoring dashboards: gpu-provisioning (live), provisioning-errors, token-latency SLO.
Alice: I'll coordinate with Sales to delay partner test by 1 hour if we need extra runway.
Ben: ping finance to confirm budget delta for preemptible vs reserved during spike.
Clara: ops will prep baked AMI images tonight. ETA 22:00 PT.
Dom: great. If no objections in next 2 hours I'll request the autoscaler change and kick the canary.
Ben: :+1:
Erin: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: note: scheduled alerting changes will be applied after canary start.
